reviews.comment: No microphone and heavy accent, completely impossible to understand most of the time. Only reads off the slides and is completely unhelpful. You will learn basically everything on your own. The best thing I got out of his lectures was a nap.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice man but his accent is genuinely incomprehensible. His lecture slides aren't great either. Most people I knew either dropped him if they had the chance or snuck into another professor's lectures just to get a handle on the material. If you're stuck with Kamon like I was, prepare to teach yourself basically everything about the course.

He's a nice professor, but it was very difficult for me to understand a single word he said and the slides were messy, but you could access the other prof slides. Thankfully there is a 30% grade outside of exams and adjusted for a C>=65. I basically had to teach this whole class myself due to this. I recommend taking someone else if possible.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. He is very qualified in physics but YOU WILL have to teach EVERYTHING to yourself. He is impossible to understand both because of his accent and because he mumbles everything. This is already a difficult class and you will double the workload if you have him.

If you are unlucky enough to be forced to take Dr. Kamons PHYS 206 be prepared to learn all of PHYS by yourself. Im sure you have seen it all over this page but it is completely impossible to understand him. He is very quiet and mumbles through all of his lectures, and on top of his accent it is impossible to learn anything in lecture.
Great guy. Was always ready to answer my questions. Well versed in the subject matter.
if youre reading this youre probably stuck with Teruki, GOOD LUCK. I chose to sneak into another profs class for lecture as there was never 100% attendance. this was the only way i learned anything.
This is not a good professor. RMP, do not delete this review.
I'm sure this professor is a great guy, but the speech barrier was a huge challenge. I pretty much has to self teach myself the entire class and it was very, very difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm sure Kamon is a fine guy, but it doesn't much matter if he can only mutter at one word a second in his heavy Korean accent. You will not get anything from lectures, but you will have to be there anyways. His grading is also oddly variable. Would not recommend to anyone under any condition. Avoid his class like the plague.

I urge everyone to listen to the other reviews and run. Run as fast as you can. It is actually impossible to understand anything he says through his accent, he teaches only from an outdated slideshow that is utter nonsense, and does iClicker so if you're scrounging for points to keep a good grade or even pass, you have to go to a useless lecture.

Run. Not worth your time. I had to teach myself the whole course (hours of my life gone) and after a while I didn't even bother showing up to class. He is a nice guy, but he is impossible to understand and his slides and examples are so disorganized that even simple concepts looked like hell. It took extreme effort on my part to get an A.

Oh poor Professor Kamon, half of our class was on aggie schedule builder trying to switch into another section DAY 1. He seems nice but has an extremely thick accent and also really poorly organized slides. I had to teach myself the entire class, forming a study group helped tremendously because I didn't learn a single thing in lectures.
Difficult and sometimes impossible to understand during class. I basically have to self teach myself. He also uses Pearson for  homework, which is a nightmare in and of itself. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He historically has one of the lowest GPA averages and he assigns an insane amount of homework for PHYS 206 University. He usually just lectures in his chair off the powerpoint and doesn't really teach. He also struggles to speak english but is very nice in office hours.
Dr. Teruki is a super nice prof, but his accent did make it difficult to understand the material. he was super accessible outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take SUPER nice guy, impossible to understand. He's way too smart to be teaching this course. All he does is read off slides (prob can do in his sleep) and they are VERY poorly made. Iclicker is required but if you look at the attendance it'll say there is only 30 of 130 students present because most people would rather learn somewhere else.
You cannot understand a word he says so lecture is pointless, which is hard because he also takes attendance for a grade. Basically it is a waste of time. do not take!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This guy does not speak English if you get him either drop or quit showing up to class.

Dr. Kamon was very sweet in office hours, and truly wanted to help his students. Unfortunately, his lectures were difficult to hear, so going tended to be a waste of time. Most of the exams were fair, but the department completely changed the format and style of the third one, which led to my Q drop. Endless amounts of homework in all 201 classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Hardest A I've ever had to work for in undergrad. I stopped going to classes in Feb and just taught myself because lectures were useless. I used YouTube to learn basic concepts, then practiced with the practice exams. HW is time-consuming - just try and complete instead of fully understanding every question. Try and do ALL practice exams.

He seems like a nice guy, but man it's so hard to understand him lecture, or present I should say, his slides. He works out no problems, rather shows you solutions. Slides have okay concepts, but they're not the best. Iclicker sucks, and MP is just time consuming. Exams are luckily just like the previous ones. He should be the last resort
Dropped it after the first day because there's no point in trying to understand what he is saying.

This professor seems really nice but only about 4 people would go to his class because it was impossible to understand him. While it is not his fault that he has a thick accent, his slides were not much better. He jumbled lots of information, never really making it clear what was expected. If you take him, do the homework! And get outside help.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DONT take physics at TAMU. You used to be able to rely on the practice exams because you are not taught adequately by any of the professors. They decided to completely change the exam format 3/4 of the way through the semester. Save yourself the tears and take it at a community college. You can't understand Kamon.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's legitimately useless as a teacher. You're gonna end up teaching yourself physics as the lectures are so utterly worthless. You're better off just taking physics at a local community college over the summer and transferring the credit

Super nice dude, wants to see his student's succeed. Unfortunately I couldn't understand him until halfway through the semester as his accent is heavy and I had to get used to it. Very willing to work with students outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lovely man. Liked physics a bit more because of his caring and helpful nature.

Loved taking physics with this specific teacher mainly because of his personality. His students' wellbeing comes first. He mainly cares if you have learned the material or not. He is very good at responding to emails. A professor that finally made me feel like I mattered. Deserves all the recognition and praise. He's there to help.
This prof is extremely hard to understand. His accent is very heavy and tests are 80% of your grade. You will learn mostly from the homework and youtube :/

Prof Kamon is a nice guy but his accent is EXTREMELY hard to understand. Dozens of my classmates have said that they understand less than half of what he says in lectures. On top of that, lecture power points are so disorganized that I can't get any info out of them. Clicker quizzes are often really difficult, and are how he takes attendance.

Dr. Kamon is sweet, but not a good prof. If you never attend a lecture you'll be just fine. Made an A in this class because of A+ tutoring and SI. Andrew and Ali are the best. Work the practice problems from those tutoring sessions and don't pay attention to the homework or book. Massive curves on the exams as well. 80 and up  A, 60 and up  B.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kamon is pretty difficult to understand while he is lecturing. That being said, he is very kind and helpful if you go to his office hours/talk to him one-on-one. The exams are curved heavily (C's get curved to A's). If you do the homework (like, actually do it) the exams aren't bad at all. I only did the homework and got consistent Bs and Cs.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All the other ratings on here had many thumbs down but they are correct. His accent is very thick and hard to understand. He is a nice man but not a great prof. The tests are now under a common exam so going to his lectures does not matter. So far for this semester, he has curved really hard so that is a benefit.

His tests are comprised of 3-5 questions worth lots of points, and a few smaller questions based on his lectures. I'd recommend going to those if you can but you won't miss too much. He gives a lot of feedback on how the class did on tests, and grades partial credit. Lots of homework, but very understanding. He gives a HUGE formula sheet for tests.

I received a better grade than I excepted. This is coming from a a student who never took physics in high school.  The best tip I can give you is to get to know him, go to his office hours, study his old exams and study his power points for exams. The only real problem with him is that he has a accent and its hard to understand most of the time.
Hard to understand because of his thick accent. Attended every class and still felt lost. His tests are very hard and the hw does not help you understand anything. Avoid him at all costs!!

Attend class and office hours. If he knows you personally he will go out of his way to help you succeed. He is always respectful of the class, answers most questions in lecture, and his notes are clear (which helps with the language barrier). He is flexible with HW deadlines. Tests are exactly like the HW. HW also gives up to a 10pt bonus on exams.

can't understand him, lots of online HW, and his notes are impossible to understand as well. If you must take him, invest in a tutor and read all of the chapters. Do all of the problems in the back of the book and do all of your homework. Thats the only way you'll survive. DONT DO IT
Stay away from this guy.
HARD

He is the worst phys teacher i have ever had. He has a bad habit of making fun of students who have trouble, while he lacks the ability to clearly convey the material.  His notes are all writen on top of pwr point slides and his accent is difficult to understand. Doesnt even make up his own notes.
